prompt: Use scale bracketing to explain why neither $0.02\text{ s}$ nor $20\text{ s}$ is an acceptable estimate for the duration of a single normal human eye blink.
answer: 0.02 s is far too brief to consciously perceive (muscle contraction takes longer). 20 s is an extended period of eyes being closed (one third of a minute), far longer than a brief blink. A realistic blink duration is around 0.1 s to 0.3 s.

mark_scheme.criterion: Explains that 0.02 s is too brief / faster than eyelid muscular action / imperceptible.
Explains that 20 s is a long duration (one third of a minute) / eyes closed, far exceeding a quick blink (or states realistic duration is ~0.1 s to 0.3 s).

hints: How many blinks would happen in one second at 0.02 s per blink?
Count out 20 seconds with your eyes closed and consider whether that describes a blink.
solution:
1. 0.02 s is 20 milliseconds, which is too fast for eyelid muscular contraction and human neurological response.
2. 20 s is one third of a whole minute, representing an extended closure of the eyes rather than a momentary blink.
Realistic eye blinks take approximately 0.1 s to 0.3 s, placing both 0.02 s and 20 s outside the physically believable bracket.
teacher_walkthrough: Demonstrate the bracketing method: reject unphysically low and unphysically high extremes.
Emphasize placing the realistic value in the bracket between extremes.
